detail.abstract: We show that operationally similar central bank asset purchases can have markedly different effects. Combining security-level data on the Federal Reserve's duration-adjusted asset holdings with narrative event-based identification reveals that purchases made for accommodation strongly affect yields, while purchases made for market functioning primarily enhance liquidity. We advance a partial equilibrium model of an intermediated bond market that can reconcile these findings. When trading flow is orderly, large-scale asset purchases (LSAPs) operate through the expected supply of duration with large effects on yields. When trading flow is disorderly, LSAPs reduce dealer inventories, improve liquidity, and compress bid-ask spreads.

title: Bayesian Optimization on the Equilibrium Manifold
affiliations: University of Zurich

detail.title: Bayesian Optimization on the Equilibrium Manifold

declarations.funderStatement: Swiss National Science Foundation (SNF)

detail.abstract: Computing optimal policy in heterogeneous-agent economies is complicated by the possibility of multiple equilibria. We overcome this difficulty by showing that when the equilibrium manifold has a low-dimensional Negishi-weight parameterization, Bayesian optimization reliably finds approximate solutions and can be used to certify candidate solutions with high probability. This insight brings recent machine learning advances to bear on a core problem in macroeconomics. We apply Bayesian optimization to a dynamic economy with heterogeneous agents and climate change and compute optimal carbon taxes in this setting. Although in principle the presence of the carbon externality creates scope for multiple equilibria, we show that in an example with realistic calibration of damages competitive equilibra are most likely unique.

detail.title: Beyond the Right to Disconnect: Legal and Sociological Perspectives on Working time Regulation in the Digital Age

publicationDetails.journalName: European Trade Union Institute (ETUI) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The blurring of the boundaries between work and private life, irregular work patterns, increasing work intensity and workers' overconnectivity are emblematic of the societal and organisational changes in modern workplaces. Although existing legal frameworks offer various instruments to address these developments, they often fall short of effectively regulating and solving the conflicts they cause. In this context, the right to disconnect – commonly defined as the right to refrain from work-related communications outside working hours – has become a central element in debates on the impact of digitalisation on working conditions. This working paper aims to advance the debate on the right to disconnect by bridging a sociological understanding of current developments in working time with a legal interpretation of the limits, conceptualisation and regulation of that right. This multidisciplinary perspective allows for the development of a robust understanding of the processes of the de-standardisation of working time that are challenging the boundary between work and non-work. In addition, it informs the regulatory effort tackling overconnectivity by placing its drivers in a wider socioeconomic context. These considerations are backed with an analysis of the most recent empirical data on working time, overconnectivity and its outcomes among European workers.

title: Is the Christian Conception of Natural Law Indispensable to a Coherent Moral Theory of the State?

detail.title: Is the Christian Conception of Natural Law Indispensable to a Coherent Moral Theory of the State?
detail.abstract: The State administers positive law, but it cannot author the moral measure that makes its laws just. This paper argues that the Christian conception of natural law is indispensable to a coherent moral theory of the State. Tracing the tradition from Plato, Aristotle, and Cicero through Augustine, Aquinas, Calvin, Luther, and Hooker, and testing it against Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, and Rawls, the argument unfolds through eight concepts: justice, citizenship, statesmanship, covenant, Christian kingship, democracy, religious and civil offices, and positive law. Each requires a standard the State cannot produce for itself. Without the imago Dei and the law written on the heart, justice lapses into procedure, covenant collapses into contract, and law becomes whatever authority can enact. It closes with policy applications: the standing of persons and conscience, the economy as ordered stewardship, and constitutional restraint on institutional capture, with a natural-law reading of cy pres.

title: Camouflage: Hidden Costs When Private Equity Firms Sell Assets to Themselves
affiliations: Institute of Management Technology (IMT), Ghaziabad and Institute of Management Technology (IMT), Ghaziabad

detail.title: Camouflage: Hidden Costs When Private Equity Firms Sell Assets to Themselves
detail.abstract: Continuation vehicles (CVs) have become an increasingly important exit route in private equity as traditional exits have remained difficult, now accounting for nearly half of secondary-market activity. In these GP-led transactions, portfolio companies are transferred into a new vehicle managed by the same general partner (GP), creating inherent conflicts of interest. The GP simultaneously acts as the seller, buyer, manager, and the party responsible for determining the net asset value (NAV), making it difficult to assess whether transactions are fairly priced. This study examines whether CV transactions shift value away from existing limited partners (LPs) and evaluates how consistently governance safeguards are applied using secondary-market data, manual deal coding, and comparative case studies.

title: Contributor-Positive Public Investment: A Theoretical Model for Revenue-Generating Environmental Justice in Industrial Communities

detail.title: Contributor-Positive Public Investment: A Theoretical Model for Revenue-Generating Environmental Justice in Industrial Communities
detail.abstract: Traditional economic models for externalities-including Pigouvian taxation, Coasean bargaining, and public-goods theory-assume that environmental regulation and redistribution impose net costs on contributors. This paper proposes a new theoretical model, ContributorPositive Public Investment (CPPI), which describes conditions under which compensatory contributions by advantaged actors generate public-good improvements so large that contributors themselves become better off than under the status quo. The model builds upon and extends Kaldor-Hicks efficiency, the Porter Hypothesis, and endogenous growth theory by requiring actual compensation, demonstrating contributor positivity, and identifying revenue-generating mechanisms within the public good itself. Using the Suncor Energy refinery in Commerce City, Colorado as a case study, the paper demonstrates how state-funded emissions-capture systems could create substantial public-health benefits while generating recoverable industrial byproducts. The paper argues that existing externality theory is incomplete in environmental justice contexts and that a new operational model is needed to describe situations where redistribution and public-good investment create mutual gains that exceed the cost of compensation. The analysis is grounded in federal regulatory data, including the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's 2024 Notice of Violation against Suncor, which documents over 9,000 Clean Air Act violations and validates the case for intervention.

title: Animal Magnetism: A Bull-Bear Polarisation Model of Endogenous Market Volatility
affiliations: Averisera Ltd

detail.title: Animal Magnetism: A Bull-Bear Polarisation Model of Endogenous Market Volatility
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces animal magnetism: a structural model of market volatility inspired by two classical ideas, Keynes's animal spirits and Anderson's principle that "more is different". Keynes gives the economic intuition: markets are moved not only by calculation, but also by confidence, fear, positioning, liquidity pressure, and the urge to act under uncertainty. Anderson gives the physical intuition: when many simple components interact, collective behaviour can emerge that is not visible at the level of the individual component.

We model unresolved bullish and bearish market pressures as interacting binary variables in an Ising-type hidden layer. Their aggregate state is the hidden bull--bear polarisation. When these pressures weakly interact, the market remains balanced and well anchored. When interaction strengthens, the market can become crowded, reactive, and fragile. Near the critical threshold, small disturbances can be amplified because the hidden state has lost resistance.

Coupling this hidden pressure layer to prices gives a structural stochastic-volatility model in which volatility clustering, fat-tailed returns, regime changes, and crash-like transitions arise as different visible consequences of the same hidden interaction structure. An empirical illustration from 2005--2026 constructs an animal-magnetism fragility score from visible stress, one-sided pressure, hidden activity, shock amplification, and loss of effective diversity. High-fragility days are followed by substantially higher realised variance, larger drawdown stress, and stronger common-mode concentration.

The result is a distinction between ordinary volatility and structural fragility. Market risk depends not only on how much prices are moving, but on the hidden collective state in which the next shock arrives.

title:
Circular Remediation:

Financial Feasibility and Real Options Analysis

of an Integrated PFAS–Microplastics Facility

detail.title:
Circular Remediation:

Financial Feasibility and Real Options Analysis

of an Integrated PFAS–Microplastics Facility
detail.abstract:
This study presents a comprehensive financial feasibility analysis of an integrated per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and microplastics remediation and resource recovery facility, employing advanced financial engineering techniques to evaluate project viability under regulatory uncertainty. Using a 20-year discounted cash flow model calibrated against three comparable infrastructure projects-the Orange County Water District PFAS program, the Philadelphia Northeast Water Pollution Control Plant biogas cogeneration system, and the L'Oréal-Ashland renewable natural gas offtake agreement-we estimate a base-case net present value (NPV) of $83.78 million at an 8% weighted average cost of capital (WACC) over a 20-year project life.

The analysis incorporates four methodological refinements to prior estimates: a 20% capital expenditure escalation to $72 million, a 25% operating cost adjustment to $5.0 million annually, segregation of microbial fuel cell (MFC) technology as a contingent real option, and a 40% material recovery revenue haircut. We apply Black–Scholes European call option pricing to value the MFC add-on at $4.41 million, demonstrating that technological uncertainty enhances option value through positive vega. A 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation with correlated stochastic variables yields a mean NPV of $74.45 million, 100% probability of positive NPV, and a Sharpe ratio of 3.30 (3.85 with RFCR).

The study evaluates tax credit integration under the Inflation Reduction Act, modeling MACRS depreciation, a 30% Investment Tax Credit ($21.6 million), and Production Tax Credits ($1.35 million annually), yielding an after-tax NPV of $41.78 million and an effective tax rate of 12.4%. We introduce a four-tier Ring-Fenced Contingency Reserve (RFCR) of $20.2 million, adapted from UK infrastructure practice, which improves the 95% Value-at-Risk from $37.49 million to $48.22 million and reduces distress probability from 4.2% to 0.8%.

Environmental justice analysis employs a Gini-adjusted Social NPV methodology, estimating social value at $158.3 million with 47% of benefits accruing to disadvantaged communities—exceeding the Justice40 threshold. Governance is embedded throughout via an independent Risk Committee, quarterly Contingency Dashboard, and unanimous-consent protocols for Tier 3 and Tier 4 reserve drawdowns, ensuring that financial resilience and distributional equity are structurally co-designed rather than appended ex post.

Comparative case calibration validates all major assumptions against realized project outcomes. A critical robustness result undergirds the entire investment thesis: the Minimum Viable Scale (MVS) analysis demonstrates that the project retains positive NPV even if mature revenue falls to 67% of base-case projections—equivalent to $14.2 million annually rather than $21.2 million. At this threshold, NPV remains positive at $1.10 million, confirming that the facility is not a marginal venture dependent on optimistic demand assumptions. This 33% revenue cushion, combined with the RFCR's $20.2 million four-tier buffer, creates a dual-layer safety net: operational underperformance must exceed one-third of projected revenue before the project approaches value destruction, and even then the contingency reserve provides 18–24 months of debt-service coverage. For municipal-backed infrastructure with fiduciary obligations to ratepayers and taxpayers, this structural resilience is the defining feature that distinguishes a speculative greenfield project from a bankable public asset.

title: The Nigerian Power System in Transition: Regulation, Markets and Institutions
affiliations: University of Abuja, Nigeria - Department of Economics

detail.title: The Nigerian Power System in Transition: Regulation, Markets and Institutions
detail.abstract: Nigeria operates the largest power system in West Africa and carries the largest electricity access deficit in the world, with an estimated 86 million people without access to electricity. Between 2023 and 2026 the country rebuilt the legal and institutional architecture of that system: a constitutional alteration establishing concurrent federal and state competence over electricity, the Electricity Act 2023, the separation of system operation from transmission ownership through the creation of the Nigerian Independent System Operator, and the transfer of regulatory oversight of intrastate markets to fifteen states. This paper provides a complete regulatory economics assessment of the Nigerian power system after these reforms, written for policymakers, regulators, sector professionals and investors. It proceeds through five connected analyses corresponding to the analytical blocks of the Executive Programme on Regulation of the Power Sector: the theory and principles of regulation applied to Nigeria's institutional history; the economics of generation adequacy, dispatch and the wholesale market; the regulation of the transmission network; distribution and end-user pricing under the service-based tariff framework and the partial tariff freeze; and the emerging architecture of multi-level regulatory institutions. A dedicated section translates the analysis into the risk allocation that investors face. The paper's central argument is that the binding constraint on the Nigerian power system is no longer legal design but the alignment of prices, subsidy obligations and institutional capacity across two tiers of regulation. The reforms have resolved jurisdictional risk; payment risk remains the frontier.

title: Price-Domain Stochastic Volatility: Exit Times, New Estimators, and Portfolio Applications
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business, George Mason University and

detail.title: Price-Domain Stochastic Volatility: Exit Times, New Estimators, and Portfolio Applications
detail.abstract: We introduce price-domain volatility (pdv), a class of volatility models whose fundamental observable is the exit time τ i , the time for the log-price to travel a fixed threshold h, rather than the squared return over a fixed clock interval. Every time-domain model-garch, har, realised variance-inherits a common structural flaw: a crash of size m amplifies the variance estimate by m^2 and takes O(ln m) periods to revert. When the S&P 500 fell 9.2% in 36 minutes and recovered in 20 (the 2010 Flash Crash), garch-based risk systems stayed elevated for eight hours. The pdv class avoids this by recording how fast prices move rather than how far: a crash of m thresholds enters as m bounded events of amplitude O(h 2), with post-crash reversion in O(1) events independent of crash size. The class has five features relative to time-domain models. New estimators: the spatial intensity  is an exact unbiased estimator of σ 2 for every threshold and every event by Wald's optional stopping theorem, and a kernel-time duality places garch, har, and figarch in one family through a Mellin transform. Bounded crash amplitude: the threshold acts as both a noise filter and an amplitude ceiling. Constant information: the Inverse Gaussian Fisher information is constant across volatility regimes, unlike garch's Gaussian information, which shrinks during crises. Exact Bayesian inference: the Spatial Stochastic Volatility (ssv) model has a log-concave full conditional, enabling exact adaptive rejection sampling. Bubble detection: Wald's identity fails for strict local martingales, giving a nonparametric bubble test that fires eight trading days before the GameStop peak of January 2021. On 1980-2024 S&P 500 data and six individual stocks, ssv achieves 23% lower volatilityforecasting RMSE than garch, 94% jump-classification accuracy against 85%, a Sharpe ratio of 1.11 against 0.79 under the Merton rule (160 bps annually), a 1.2-day lead over the VIX, and 6.5× faster reversion after the 2010 Flash Crash. The data requirement is minimal: daily closing prices suffice.

title: The Twin Conundrum: Public Morality, Justice, and Uncertainty in a Social Dilemma

detail.title: The Twin Conundrum: Public Morality, Justice, and Uncertainty in a Social Dilemma

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involved an anonymous, voluntary online survey. No personally identifiable information was collected, and participants were informed about the purpose of the research before choosing whether to participate. Participation was voluntary, and respondents could discontinue the survey at any time. Electronic informed consent was obtained prior to participation. The study was conducted independently and not under the auspices of an institution requiring formal ethics committee approval; therefore, no institutional ethics approval was sought.
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the Twin Conundrum, an original moral dilemma designed to observe how individuals make moral decisions under uncertainty and with the threat of irreversible consequences. Unlike binary-option dilemmas like the trolley problem, the Twin Conundrum presents respondents with six outcomes that span multiple moral frameworks (deontological, utilitarian, probabilistic, and retributive) while also capturing qualitative questions across a diverse demographic sample. 

The Twin Conundrum confronts respondents with a scenario where a serial killer is confirmed to be one of two identical twins, yet forensic, testimonial, or video evidence is unable to establish the guilty twin, thus forcing the respondent to decide under information asymmetry. Responses were collected using a two-phase purposive quota sampling method which helped ensure approximating global continent-based population proportions within the sample. Using a mixed analytical framework, findings revealed that nearly half of the respondents chose to acquit both twins across various demographic groups, suggesting a strong deontological preference for protecting innocence over public safety even for participants who supported flexible justice principles. The chi-square analysis revealed that age and political orientation were statistically significant predictors of outcome choice, with deontological preference rising with age in a near-linear manner, while left-leaning respondents were more likely to advocate innocence protection. Qualitative analysis revealed that Risk Aversion/Pragmatism was the most frequently occurring theme and was also well distributed across all six outcome choices, thus suggesting that probability-weighing produces morally pluralistic rather than concentrated conclusions.

The paper contributes to existing literature both methodologically and conceptually by demonstrating that apparent moral consensus on outcomes may not exist when multiple options are available to individuals and even when they do, significant disagreement exists on the principles that justify them.

title: A Bayesian Model of Mantra, Persuasion, and Detachment
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: A Bayesian Model of Mantra, Persuasion, and Detachment
detail.abstract: How does one change a belief ? We give a Bayesian account in which a disposition is a heading on the circle carrying a von Mises belief, so that the natural parameter is a planar vector whose direction is what one tends to do and whose length is conviction, and updating is vector addition. A mantra is then repeated pseudo-evidence: each utterance adds a vector, and emotion is the precision it carries. Ramakrishna's maxim, that positive injunction beats prohibition, becomes a theorem. Precision is non-negative, so the updates a mind can perform form a convex cone, the update that would negate a thought points outside it, and the nearest feasible substitute, which must represent what it would suppress, deposits positive evidence on the forbidden direction. A mind cannot subtract a thought. This raises a puzzle, since minds plainly do give up habits. We resolve it with a two-layer model in which outcome beliefs are mapped to behavioral pulls by a value function. Both layers admit only additions, but the value map is order-reversing, so a positive addition in the outcome layer, which is what a story is, produces a strict decrease in the pull of an action. A mind subtracts a direction only by adding a consequence. This is why telling someone not to smoke does nothing while telling them what smoking did to a man they knew does a great deal, and the size of the eect is Hume's likelihood ratio for testimony, damped by entrenchment. Fear is a localized threat belief that avoidance keeps starved of evidence; anxiety is a diuse one, extinguishing more slowly by a factor equal to the number of directions it is smeared across, which is why naming a fear is a precondition for curing it. Recitation is a weak periodic drive, and we show by simulation that its eect on the mind is a stochastic resonance, maximal at an intermediate level of agitation. Simulations conrm the central predictions: an agent told not to go West ends there more often than an agent told nothing, and an injunction against smoking leaves more smokers than silence while a story leaves almost none.

title: Simplifying Nature Away? Ex-Ante Evidence on the EFRAG ESRS Cuts from Three Years of European Nature Disclosures *
affiliations: University of Zurich - Department of Finance, University of Zurich, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Zurich

detail.title: Simplifying Nature Away? Ex-Ante Evidence on the EFRAG ESRS Cuts from Three Years of European Nature Disclosures *
detail.abstract: The European Commission adopted revised European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) on 3 July 2026, following EFRAG's December 2025 technical advice. Using the datapoint schedule in that technical advice, which reduces required datapoints, when material, by 61% overall and ESRS E4 biodiversity datapoints by 78%, we assess the nature-related disclosures of STOXX Europe 600 companies over FY2023-FY2025 (801 TNFD and 1,047 ESRS firm-year observations) with a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline that extends the ASKNATURE system. Three findings bear on the proposal. First, mandatory reporting delivers: ESRS disclosures carry a specificity premium of +0.13 on the unit scale (p < 0.01) and an enforceability premium of +0.16 (p < 0.01) over voluntary TNFD reporting, and ESRS E1+E2 evidence depth rises from 0.785 to 0.805 (FY2025 partial) with narrowing variance under the CSRD. Second, mandatory reporting has limits: it produces no commitment premium, the roughly 4:1 positive-to-negative sentiment skew in nature-impact reporting survives the mandate, and dual TNFD+ESRS reporters show no disclosure premium over single-framework reporters. Third, under proportional datapoint retention the simplification would erase 57% of observable ESRS evidence depth on average and 78% of E4 biodiversity evidence, collapsing the cross-sector differentiation on which institutional nature-risk screening relies. The improving climate-disclosure trend under the CSRD offers no assurance that biodiversity disclosure would survive the simplified regime. Preserving core quantitative E4 requirements, in particular the E4-5 KPIs and site-level granularity, is necessary to keep European nature reporting from reverting to the voluntary cheap-talk baseline we document.

title: State Tax Exemptions for Tribal Cultural Property
affiliations: University of Alabama - School of Law and University of Tennessee, Knoxville - Winston College of Law

detail.title: State Tax Exemptions for Tribal Cultural Property
detail.abstract: In 2026, the California legislature enacted Assembly Bill (AB) 1485, which exempts from real property transfer taxes certain transactions that return tribal land to tribes. This Essay examines AB 1485 as a model for how state tax policy can further tribal sovereignty by facilitating the return of culturally significant land to federally recognized Indian tribes. This Essay argues that state and local taxes imposed on the transfer of land to tribal governments create practical financial barriers to reacquisition, reinforcing the historic erosion of tribal land and limiting tribes' ability to protect sacred sites and sustain community life. Understanding these tax burdens within the broader legacy of allotment and dispossession, this Essay contends that other states should adopt more durable and inclusive exemptions than AB 1485. By reframing transfer tax exemptions as a state's recognition of inherent tribal sovereignty, and as a modest response to the colonial foundations of state land ownership, this Essay concludes that state tax reform can serve as a meaningful tool for states to participate in rebuilding reservation communities and in strengthening tribal-state relations.

The sine-squared transform sends any L´evy representation of a function F, with measure M ≥ 0 and drift b ≥ 0, to a Thorin representation of 1/F(√s) with density U(v) = (2π√v)−1 b+ 2sin2(x√v/2)M(dx) = (2π√v)−1Re(F′/F)(i√v). detail.abstract: This sub-study evaluates the effectiveness of an intensive Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) professional development program in enhancing primary school teachers' AI-based Pedagogical Content Knowledge (AI-PCK) and identifies the specific component that yielded the highest level of improvement. Using a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design, the study examined a sample of 142 in-service primary school teachers. Data were collected via a researcher-developed questionnaire covering 5 distinct components of AI-PCK and analyzed using paired t-tests and Cohen's d effect size. The findings confirmed a highly significant overall positive impact of the professional development program on the teachers' total AI-PCK scores (𝑝 < 0.001), accompanied by an exceptionally large effect size (𝑑 = 3.71). Learning gain analysis revealed that the fifth component-familiarity with and application of assessment rubrics-experienced the most substantial improvement, achieving the highest learning gain (2.65) and the largest individual effect size (𝑑 = 4.82). This result implies that in the era of Generative AI, the critical professional development priority for primary school teachers has shifted from content creation tools toward mastering the design of authentic, process-oriented assessment rubrics. This research offers a foundational framework for educational policymakers addressing the challenge of AI authenticity in primary education.

title: Why carbon offsets can't be fixed: Economic theory with illustrations from Australia
affiliations: University of Technology Sydney, and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Why carbon offsets can't be fixed: Economic theory with illustrations from Australia
detail.abstract: Study after study has found that carbon credit-generating projects have resulted in vastly more carbon being credited as having been abated than has actually been abated. These ‘integrity’ problems are now well-known. In response, scholars have called for improved governance and transparency of carbon credit projects and markets to ensure integrity. We argue that carbon credit markets cannot be fixed, because such markets possess a number of inherent features that conduce to over-crediting and hence low-integrity. Our argument draws primarily on neoclassical economic theory, with a particular focus on the interaction between information and incentive problems that plague carbon credit markets, supplemented by insights from political economy. We illustrate our points using Australia’s carbon credit market, which exhibits the problematic features we identify despite being one of the world’s most highly-regulated carbon credit markets. Our argument supports calls to sever the ‘offset’ relationship between project-based carbon abatement activities and emissions-intensive activities and to adopt separate national carbon accounts, and government strategies, for decarbonisation and carbon removal.

title: Mandatory ESG Disclosure and Corporate Hedging

detail.title: Mandatory ESG Disclosure and Corporate Hedging
detail.abstract: Does mandatory ESG disclosure change how firms hedge? This paper models a firm that jointly chooses hedge ratios and disclosure intensity, with disclosure operating only through the price the firm attaches to residual risk. The model yields closed-form hedge ratios and signed comparative statics, and is tested on Korea's two realized ESG-disclosure mandates (the governance report, phased in by asset tier over 2019-2024, and the environmental-information requirement binding large issuers from 2022) on a 380-firm, 3,420 firm-year panel of KOSPI issuers parsed from OpenDART filings. Group-time ATT estimates are nulls on both hedging margins for both mandates: point estimates within half a percentage point of zero on the primary margin, with confidence intervals that cap a positive response, the sign the competing disclosure channels predict, at one to six percentage points. The channel is risk-specific: mandates that leave market-risk exposure unquantified leave the hedging incentive unchanged. Korea's climate mandate, which compels that quantification from fiscal 2027 with enforcement phasing in through 2030, is the model's dated forward test.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Trading, and Financial Market Microstructure: A Systematic Literature Review
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Trading, and Financial Market Microstructure: A Systematic Literature Review
detail.abstract: The past two decades have witnessed a structural transformation in financial market microstructure: human traders have been displaced by algorithmic agents operating at microsecond timescales. This paper provides a systematic review of the academic literature on how algorithmic trading (AT), high-frequency trading (HFT), and artificial intelligence—including large language models (LLMs) and machine learning classifiers—have reshaped three foundational dimensions of market quality: liquidity provision, price discovery, and market stability. Following a PRISMA-compliant protocol, we screened 847 initial records across Web of Science, Scopus, SSRN, and Google Scholar, ultimately synthesizing 60 studies meeting pre-specified inclusion criteria. We organize the literature around three central debates. The first concerns whether algorithmic market-making constitutes genuine liquidity supply or phantom liquidity that evaporates under stress, amplifying flash crashes across equity, Treasury, and foreign exchange markets. The second examines the tension between AI-enhanced informational efficiency and systemic fragility induced by algorithmic herding, correlated machine-learning strategies, and retail-driven social media trading. The third surveys the regulatory challenge of detecting AI-facilitated market manipulation—including spoofing and quote stuffing—through natural language processing and high-frequency surveillance. Drawing on foundational contributions from Kyle (1985), Glosten and Milgrom (1985), and Budish, Cramton, and Shim (2015), we characterize the current paradigm as "algorithmic ecology"—a co-evolutionary ecosystem in which AI agents, human traders, exchanges, and regulators continuously adapt to one another's strategies. We identify a fundamental paradigm shift: market microstructure research must transition from models of rational human agents toward frameworks accommodating the strategic behavior, correlated failures, and emergent dynamics of algorithmic agents.

title: Maximum Entropy Algorithms for Predictive Rules: Blahut-Arimoto, Conditional Limits, and Iterative Scaling
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and

detail.title: Maximum Entropy Algorithms for Predictive Rules: Blahut-Arimoto, Conditional Limits, and Iterative Scaling
detail.abstract: Raking a contingency table, tilting an empirical measure onto a moment condition, allocating scarce attention across states, and quantizing a Gaussian source are four descriptions of one operation: project a baseline distribution onto a convex constraint set in relative entropy. The solution is always an exponential tilt, that tilt is always the gradient of a log-partition function, and that log-partition is always an envelope. We show that the algorithm computing it is determined by exactly two questions. Is the baseline fixed or self-consistent? Are the constraints equalities or inequalities? The answers give iterative proportional fitting, Dykstra-Bregman, Blahut-Arimoto, and majorisation, each a special case of Csiszár-Tusnády alternating minimisation. We work two canonical applications in full, the lottery problem of Stern and Cover (1989) and the rational inattention model of Sims (2003), and show that the rational inattention literature has been running Blahut-Arimoto without naming it. Two warnings emerge. Cyclic I-projection, correct on affine sets, fails silently on inequalityconstrained ones, overstating the divergence by 40% in our example. And the Hessian of mutual information with respect to a parameter is not positive semidefinite, so identification diagnostics built on it are ill-posed; the envelope representation of Polson and Scott repairs this and supplies a free certificate of weak identification.

title: How Firms Form Beliefs and the Implications for Inflation
affiliations: Harvard University and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: How Firms Form Beliefs and the Implications for Inflation
detail.abstract: Using survey data from U.S. firms, we study the primitive beliefs for price-setting: firms' forecasts of their own marginal costs. These forecasts are disconnected from CPI expectations, (over)react to current and past costs systematically, and underreact to aggregate shocks until costs move. We show that under empirically realistic cost beliefs the New Keynesian Phillips curve is steeper and less forwardlooking. Supply shocks are more inflationary because they hit costs quickly. Demand shocks are less inflationary because firms fail to anticipate future wage pressure. Forward guidance weakens at long horizons but strengthens in the near term.

title: The Regulatory Waterbed Unilateral Leverage Caps and the Contamination of a Shared Perpetual-Futures Settlement Index

detail.title: The Regulatory Waterbed Unilateral Leverage Caps and the Contamination of a Shared Perpetual-Futures Settlement Index
detail.abstract: A unilateral leverage cap on perpetual-futures contracts that are cash-settled against a shared, manipulable index can raise systemic fragility while lowering total leverage and fire-sale risk. Tightening pushes leverage to opaque offshore venues, where it degrades the shared settlement price. The harm falls on onshore positions that never moved yet settle against that price. In a 2026 calibration, tightening cuts total leverage 11% and raises index contamination 22%. Risk climbs as leverage falls. Regulatory-arbitrage and macroprudential reasoning miss this referenceprice externality. No single cap can address it. The remedy is a Tinbergen pair of instruments. Clean the index, then coordinate margins.

title: Beyond Enforcement: The Hybrid Advertising Recovery Model (HARM) as a Solution to Deadweight Loss in Digital Goods Markets

detail.title: Beyond Enforcement: The Hybrid Advertising Recovery Model (HARM) as a Solution to Deadweight Loss in Digital Goods Markets

detail.abstract: The traditional digital economy operates on a binary licensing model: users are either compliant payers or non-compliant "pirates." This rigidity creates a deadweight loss estimated at $47.5 billion annually, where potential economic value is excluded due to pricing barriers in emerging markets. This paper proposes the Hybrid Advertising Recovery Model (HARM), a framework utilizing third-degree price discrimination to monetize non-compliant users. By substituting currency with "attention friction" (advertising impressions) and "input latency" (performance degradation), firms can recover revenue from zero-marginal-cost goods without cannibalizing premium markets. Case studies of Adobe Systems, Tencent Interactive Entertainment, Sony Interactive Entertainment, and Microsoft Corporation demonstrate the model's efficacy in converting shadow economies into legitimate, measurable asset classes. The paper further argues that the strategic value of HARM extends beyond immediate revenue to the capture of "Behavioral Sovereignty Data" from the Global South-diverse workflow data currently invisible to AI training pipelines.

title: The General Framework of AI Economics: Computation, Data, and the Limits of Formalized Intelligence
affiliations: Tsinghua University and

detail.title: The General Framework of AI Economics: Computation, Data, and the Limits of Formalized Intelligence
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is the first general-purpose technology automating cognitive labor—the core of human productivity—but existing economic frameworks fail to explain its unique cost structure, extreme scale economies, and fundamental physical/logical limits. This paper develops a unified theory of AI economics grounded in computability theory and the ontological distinction between formalized computational systems and human consciousness. We propose a six-factor framework partitioning AI into two incommensurable layers: a formalized layer (compute, algorithms, data, parameters, energy) bound by Turing computability and thermodynamics, and a hyper-Turing layer (human consciousness) as the sole source of paradigm shifts. We make three core contributions: (1) formalize the training-inference cost migration theory, deriving the natural monopoly property of foundation models; (2) reinterpret scaling laws as production functions incorporating consciousness as a non-substitutable factor, explaining the AI productivity paradox; (3) prove three unbreakable "cages" constraining all AI systems, demonstrating consciousness as the irreducible source of value creation. Our framework explains key AI economic phenomena including platform monopolies, limits to AI self-evolution, and the tiered structure of token markets. We further develop a downstream value-augmentation theory of token pricing, demonstrating that token value is anchored by downstream industrial productivity gains rather than production costs, and that quality thresholds create discontinuous price gaps between frontier and commodity tokens. We conclude with testable empirical implications and targeted policy recommendations.

title: Private Entity, Public Perks: Examining the Accountability of the BCCI as a Registered Society in Light of Subsidised Public Land and State Support
affiliations: Quantum University

detail.title: Private Entity, Public Perks: Examining the Accountability of the BCCI as a Registered Society in Light of Subsidised Public Land and State Support
detail.abstract:
The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), registered as a society under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, 1975, occupies a paradoxical position in Indian law and governance. It is the world's wealthiest cricket board, wielding monopolistic control over the sport that functions as India's de facto national pastime, yet it claims the legal identity of a private, autonomous organisation beyond the reach of public accountability laws. This paper examines the tension between that private claim and the substantial public benefits the BCCI enjoys, including subsidised government land at nominal lease rates, tax exemptions under Section 11 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, deployment of state police and administrative machinery, and the tacit backing of both the Central Government and state governments.

The central argument of this paper is that the BCCI's enjoyment of significant public resources — quantified in indirect terms at over Rs 2,100 crore in tax exemptions alone between 1997 and 2007[1] — combined with its exercise of functions of national importance, creates a compelling legal and constitutional case for treating it as a 'public authority' subject to transparency obligations. The paper employs doctrinal legal research, drawing on primary sources including Supreme Court judgments, Law Commission reports, Parliamentary debates, and Central Information Commission (CIC) orders.

The principal findings are: first, that the Supreme Court has recognised BCCI as performing 'public functions' amenable to writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, even while declining to classify it as 'State' under Article 12; second, that the Law Commission's 275th Report (2018) and the CIC's 2018 order supported RTI applicability, a conclusion reversed by the CIC in 2026; and third, that the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, by limiting RTI applicability to bodies receiving direct government grants, has created a policy gap that shields the BCCI from meaningful accountability. The paper recommends a hybrid regulatory model that conditions public benefits on conditional transparency obligations, alongside targeted legislative reform to the RTI Act, 2005.


 


[1]Law Commission of India, 275th Report: 'Legal Framework: BCCI vis-a-vis Right to Information Act' (April 2018) [hereinafter 'LCI 275th Report'] 3-5.

title: Can LLMs Hire Fairly? Racial Bias in Resume Screening
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School,  and

detail.title: Can LLMs Hire Fairly? Racial Bias in Resume Screening
detail.abstract: We audit fourteen mainstream large language models (LLMs) for hiring discrimination using the paired-resume methodology of Kline, Rose, and Walters (2022). The sole 2023-vintage model reproduces the pro-White callback gap documented in field experiments on labor market discrimination (+2.12 pp, significant at the 1% level). Every model released in 2024 or after shows either a null gap or a significant pro-Black reversal (up to-3.01 pp). The same pattern holds on the gender axis. Based on 24,024 paired postings per model across 14 models, our results document a reversal in the direction of algorithmic hiring bias across model generations.

title: A Mortality-Adjusted Discount Rate for Intangible Asset Valuation: Theoretical Derivation, Sector Calibration, and Preliminary Empirical Evidence

detail.title: A Mortality-Adjusted Discount Rate for Intangible Asset Valuation: Theoretical Derivation, Sector Calibration, and Preliminary Empirical Evidence
detail.abstract: Every conventional discount rate used in intangible asset valuation - WACC, levered cost of equity (Ke), and unlevered cost of equity (Ku) - is derived from observable equity prices of firms that carry debt. Even Ku, the theoretically cleanest of the three, is estimated by unlevering the Ke of comparable companies, thereby importing their capital structures into the asset-level rate. This paper proposes Ko, a mortality adjusted operational discount rate derived entirely from risk-free rates, market risk premia, and empirically calibrated sector survival curves - with substantially reduced dependence on capital structure: the mortality premium πmort and the risk-free rate Rf require no leverage data, while the systematic component βu×ERP retains a residual dependence on sector comparables’ leverage via standard unlevering. Ko is formally derived as Ko = Rf + βu × ERP + πmort, where πmort = −ln[S(T+H)/S(T)]/H is the conditional mortality premium, S(t) is the Weibull survival function calibrated from establishment cohort data, T is the firm's age at valuation, and H is the asset's useful life horizon. We calibrate Ko across 19 NAICS sectors using 30 years of U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics cohort data. Cross-sectoral mortality premia range from 0.21% (Healthcare) to 21.49% (Transportation and Warehousing), producing Ko values between 7.40% and 28.68% against a sector-average Ku of 7.19%. The differential in intangible asset value between Ko and Ku ranges from 0.9% to 53.9% depending on sector mortality profile and firm age. These figures apply to assets with full operational continuity dependence (transferability factor φ=1); for separable assets such as patents and registered trademarks, the effective mortality premium scales as φ×πmort where φ∈[0,1]. Illustrative application to the NovaDerm Therapeutics LLC case (NAICS 325620) demonstrates that Ko converges within 1.73 percentage points of the Duff & Phelps build-up rate - achieved through a structurally independent derivation that requires no leverage assumption, no comparable company selection. The systematic risk component retains a residual dependence on sector comparables via standard unlevering, acknowledged in Section 2.1. Ko operationalizes the survival-conditioned discounting established by Skogsvik (2006) and Damodaran’s truncation-risk analysis, extending it to the intangible-asset PPA level with a sector-cohort calibration and a transferability adjustment. Ko separates and makes observable the capital structure contamination identified in purchase price allocation practice under IFRS 3 and ASC 805. Ko further provides a tractable, auditable rate for intangible asset valuation in M&A contexts.

title: Deep Learning Architectures for Multi-Asset ETF Return Prediction and Portfolio Allocation: MLP, CNN-GAF, LSTM, GRU, and Ensemble Methods
affiliations: , University of Hafr AlBatin and ECOVIS Saudi Arabia (ECOVIS AL SABTI)

detail.title: Deep Learning Architectures for Multi-Asset ETF Return Prediction and Portfolio Allocation: MLP, CNN-GAF, LSTM, GRU, and Ensemble Methods
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the comparative predictive performance of five deep learning architectures-Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Convolutional Neural Network with Gramian Angular Field encoding (CNN-GAF), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and an MLP-LSTM ensemble-applied to 25-day-ahead cumulative log-return prediction across three exchange-traded funds (SPY, TLT, GLD) spanning 2008-2022. Using a 15-dimensional feature vector comprising five technical indicators over an optimal three-day lag window identified through time-series cross-validation, we find that no architecture achieves consistently positive out-of-sample R 2 , consistent with the Efficient Market Hypothesis. However, directional accuracy exceeds the 50% random baseline for all models on equity and fixed-income ETFs. The GRU architecture delivers the highest overall directional accuracy (65.45% for SPY), outperforming LSTM on all metrics. CNN-GAF achieves the best single-asset directional accuracy (67.07% for SPY) by capturing angular momentum patterns in compact 3 × 3 Gramian Angular Summation Field images. A backtested portfolio strategy employing GRU predictions with proportional position sizing generates a total return of +59.29% and a Sharpe ratio of 0.683 over the test period (2018-2022), substantially outperforming an equal-weight buy-and-hold benchmark (+21.48%, Sharpe 0.457) while maintaining a lower maximum drawdown (-22.09% vs.-22.78%). These results demonstrate that GRU-based directional signals with return-magnitude-proportional position sizing offer a tractable and robust framework for short-horizon multi-asset allocation.

title: Credit Composition, Equity Market Performance, and Crash Risk

detail.title: Credit Composition, Equity Market Performance, and Crash Risk

contentType.other: Submitted to Journal of Money, Credit and Banking

detail.abstract: This paper studies how household and business credit expansions differentially affect equity market performance. We show that the composition of private credit is central for asset pricing and financial stability. Expansions in household credit predict lower subsequent stock market returns and a higher probability of market crashes, whereas business credit expansions also forecast lower returns but are not associated with elevated crash risk. These patterns suggest that household credit booms are linked to mispricing and heightened downside tail risk, while business credit booms primarily reflect cyclical variation in investment opportunities and expected risk premia. We further document that these effects vary systematically across countries: the crashrisk implications of household credit are concentrated in advanced economies, while credit expansions in emerging markets primarily operate through business credit with weaker links to crash risk. Finally, we show that the relationship between credit expansions and crash risk depends on the macroprudential policy environment, with policy interventions weakening the adverse effects of household credit growth.

title: Revenue at Risk from AI Displacement: A Methodology for Quantifying the Financial Exposure Created by Systematic Brand Displacement in AI Recommendation Flows

detail.title: Revenue at Risk from AI Displacement: A Methodology for Quantifying the Financial Exposure Created by Systematic Brand Displacement in AI Recommendation Flows
detail.abstract:
This working paper introduces Revenue at Risk from AI Displacement (RaR-AID) as a formally defined category of enterprise financial exposure and presents a structured methodology for its calculation. As AI systems become the primary intermediary in an increasing proportion of commercial purchase decisions, the systematic displacement of brands before the final recommendation creates a quantifiable revenue exposure that does not yet appear in most enterprise risk frameworks. Drawing on the AIVO Standard empirical corpus of 1,427 structured brand probes across ten industries and four major AI platforms, and confirmed by three independent research programmes published in 2026, this paper establishes that 87.3% of brands present at the first turn of a multi-turn AI buying conversation are displaced by a competitor before the final purchase recommendation, and that 75.7% of brand facts possessed by the model are not deployed at the decision turn. These findings constitute a systematic and measurable financial exposure for brands with material AI-mediated category revenue. 
The paper presents the Revenue at Risk from AI Displacement (RaR-AID) calculation methodology, consisting of three inputs-Category-relevant Annual Revenue (CAR), AImediated Purchase Influence Rate (APIR), and Measured AI Displacement Rate (ADR)-and their combination into a financially quantified board-level exposure figure. A reference engagement in the Financial Services sector is used to illustrate the methodology's application. The paper argues that RaR-AID constitutes a material risk exposure suitable for board-level reporting alongside established risk categories including credit risk, commodity price risk, and supply chain exposure.

detail.abstract: The historical "Socialist Calculation Debate" argued that decentralized market pricing is the only viable mechanism for resource allocation, yet the emergence of advanced artificial intelligence and algorithmic planning has reopened this discourse. This paper addresses the critical problem of how to computationally model a post-scarcity, moneyless economy-specifically the Value Consensus Currency (VCC) framework. To achieve this, we deploy a multi-agent simulation using the Llama-3.1-8b model as a proxy for boundedly rational socioeconomic actors. The simulation operates over a 100-epoch cycle across three distinct configurations: a balanced Baseline, a Climate Shock, and a Consumer Hegemony. Our results computationally suggest that while algorithmic resource allocation is mathematically stable under balanced demographic conditions, the system remains highly vulnerable to psychological heuristics. Without supreme, non-derogable ecological constraints (jus cogens), the simulated human-like short-term biases and unchecked consumption preferences of the agents consistently tend to trigger severe ecological degradation.

title: Philosophy and Science: The Civilizatory Contribution of Philosophy

detail.title: Philosophy and Science: The Civilizatory Contribution of Philosophy
detail.abstract:
Science and philosophy emerged from a common intellectual tradition but gradually evolved toward distinct civilizatory functions. Science seeks to increase humanity’s knowledge of reality through the construction of progressively more powerful explanatory models. Philosophy seeks to integrate that knowledge into comprehensive visions of existence, humanity, and civilization.

The distinctive contribution of philosophy lies not in empirical explanation but in civilizatory orientation. Great philosophical systems are not merely theories about reality; they are proposals concerning how human beings should understand themselves and how they ought to live together.

Science expands human capabilities. Philosophy expands humanity’s possible futures. Civilization depends on both.

title: Bayesian Asymptotics: Merging, Martingales, and Moderate Deviations
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and

detail.title: Bayesian Asymptotics: Merging, Martingales, and Moderate Deviations
detail.abstract: We give a unified account of the asymptotic theory of Bayesian inference, organized around a single object: the local log-likelihood-ratio random field. Reading the posterior as a tilt of the prior by this field clarifies why the same machinery delivers consistency, merging of opinions, Bernstein–von Mises (BvM) normality, information-theoretic redundancy bounds, and largedeviation behaviour. We assemble the classical results—Kolmogorov’s measure-theoretic sufficiency, Blackwell–Dubins merging, Doob’s martingale convergence, Walker, Dawid and Heyde– Johnstone posterior normality, Ibragimov–Has’minskii regularity classes, and Berk’s misspecified limits—and the information-theoretic dual of Clarke–Barron and Lindley. We then develop two strands. First, we make explicit the martingale structure of the marginal likelihood and the Bayes factor: the Bayes factor of two simple-prior models is a nonnegative test martingale, so Ville’s inequality yields anytime-valid Bayesian tests and links to the theory of e-values. Second, we place the moderate deviation principle (MDP) for the posterior—a Gaussian-rate sharpening of BvM between the n −1/2 central-limit and O(1) relative-entropy scales—inside the local-field picture, and follow it through to e-values and Bayes-factor testing. The MDP is itself part of the broader identity we abbreviate as de Finetti + Sanov = Bayes: exchangeability furnishes a prior over limiting frequencies, Sanov’s theorem furnishes the exponential decay, and the posterior is the resulting Gibbs tilt; an “inverse Sanov” (Gibbs conditioning) reads the conditional law back off the rate function. We close with modern applications—sparse and high-dimensional shrinkage, variational and simulation-based posteriors, and over-parametrized models—where these limits are sharp, fail, or remain open.

title: The Macroeconomic Limits of Mandated Wage Floors: Labor Market Compression, Welfare Traps, and the Technological Deflation Alternative

detail.title: The Macroeconomic Limits of Mandated Wage Floors: Labor Market Compression, Welfare Traps, and the Technological Deflation Alternative
detail.abstract: This paper presents a structural critique of minimum wage legislation as a mechanism for sustainable poverty alleviation. We argue that conventional labor policy frequently suffers from a foundational nominal illusion, treating fiat currency as an independent source of wealth rather than a medium of exchange for underlying real value. By analyzing the macroeconomic feedback loops triggered by artificial price floors, this paper maps two distinct systemic paths. First, we outline an unconstrained labor price readjustment resulting in a wage-price spiral. Second, we evaluate a policy-constrained compression trap that structurally downgrades middle-class purchasing power. Finally, we contrast these outcomes with empirical evidence from key modern case studies, including Seattle's $15 mandate and Germany's statutory implementation, demonstrating that productivity-driven technological deflation represents the only viable mechanism for sustainably increasing real wages and societal abundance without distorting market incentives.

detail.abstract: Tokenized stocks emerge as an innovative gateway to the ownership of foreign assets that otherwise would not be accessible to many investors worldwide. We find that tracking errors increase with return volatility, market-wide uncertainty and weaker alignment between token and equity returns. Moreover, mis-tracking is more pronounced for firms with higher valuations, greater market risk exposure, and elevated short-selling activity.
